en.intro: After seeing the cosmic form, Arjuna names the forces of nature and bows again and again. Listen to how he addresses the Lord.
en.notice: The word pratapamahatvam in the next verse points to boundless power, but here Arjuna fixes his gaze on the great ancestor, the source of Brahma, showing that the creator and the destroyer are one.
en.next: Arjuna bows to this boundless power from every direction, acknowledging that it is all around him.
en.meaning: You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and the great ancestor. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again.

hi.intro: विश्वरूप देखकर अर्जुन प्रकृति की शक्तियों को भगवान का रूप मानते हैं और बार-बार प्रणाम करते हैं। सुनिए, वे प्रभु को किस रूप में पुकारते हैं।
hi.meaning: आप ही वायु, यमराज, अग्नि, वरुण, चन्द्रमा, दक्ष आदि प्रजापति और प्रपितामह ब्रह्माजीके भी पिता हैं। आपको हजारों बार नमस्कार हो, नमस्कार हो और फिर भी आपको बार-बार नमस्कार हो।
hi.notice: यहाँ प्रपितामह शब्द का अर्थ ब्रह्मा के भी पिता है। अर्जुन इस विशाल रूप में ब्रह्मा के स्रोत को भी एक ही मानते हैं, जो इस रूप की विशालता को दर्शाता है।
hi.next: अर्जुन इस असीम शक्ति को हर ओर से प्रणाम करते हैं और स्वीकार करते हैं कि यह सर्वव्यापी है।

en.intro: After seeing the cosmic form, Arjuna names the forces of nature and bows again and again. Listen to how he addresses the Lord.
en.body: You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and the great ancestor. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again. The word pratapamahatvam in the next verse points to boundless power, but here Arjuna fixes his gaze on the great ancestor, the source of Brahma, showing that the creator and the destroyer are one. Arjuna bows to this boundless power from every direction, acknowledging that it is all around him.

issues: meaning_changed: "और फिर भी आपको बारबार नमस्कार हो" (The phrase 'और फिर भी' (and yet/still) introduces a contrastive meaning ('still bowing again and again') that is not present in the original Sanskrit 'पुनश्च भूयः अपि' (and again and again). This changes the tone from repeated reverence to a sense of reluctant or surprising continuation, which is unsupported by the source.)
